# Module `process`

process - run external commands.

Thin wrappers over the runtime's `__vyb_exec_*` functions in
`runtime/vyb_runtime.c`. A full command line (with shell metacharacters,
pipelines, and redirection) is passed through `sh -c`, so callers supply
trusted command strings.

Fallible execution follows the engine-wide `T?` shape (PROGRAMMERS_GUIDE
§3.16): `exec_run` returns `Int?` -- absent when the command could not be
launched, present holding its exit status otherwise -- and `exec_output`
returns `String?` -- absent only on launch failure, present holding stdout
(which may legitimately be empty). The old `-1`/`""` sentinels could not
distinguish launch failure from a real exit status / empty output. `exec_status`
(the read-only probe) still reports the last child's exit status as a plain Int.

Running a shell command reaches outside the managed model, so Vyb gates the
two executing helpers behind an explicit `freedom` block: a caller must write
`freedom { exec_run("...") }` (or `freedom { exec_output("...") }`). The
read-only `exec_status` probe stays ungated and is callable from any code.

<a id="sym-exec_output"></a>
### `exec_output` · fn

```
exec_output(cmd<String>)<String?> ->
```

Capture `cmd`'s stdout; returns `String?` -- present holding the output (which
may be empty) when it launched, absent when it could not be launched. The exit
status is available from `exec_status()`.

<a id="sym-exec_status"></a>
### `exec_status` · fn

```
exec_status()<Int> ->
```

The last child's exit status (read-only probe; 0..255, or -1 if none yet or a
launch failure). Works from ordinary code.

<a id="sym-proc_error"></a>
### `proc_error` · fn

```
proc_error(operation<String>, command<String>)<ProcError> ->
```

Build a `ProcError` for the named `operation` on `command`. Typical use is
shaping an absent `exec_run`/`exec_output` into a fail:
  match (exec_output(cmd)) { s -> ..., ? -> { fail proc_error("output", cmd) } }

<a id="sym-procerror"></a>
### `ProcError` · struct

```
struct ProcError {
```

Fields:

- `operation<String>`
- `command<String>`
- `message<String>`

A shared error value for escalating a failed process launch into the fail/trap
framework. `operation` names the failing call ("run" / "output"); `command` is
the command that failed; `message` carries a diagnostic (empty when the runtime
recorded none).
